dialog.body: City of Newport Utilities, billing, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, so I just got a reminder notice? For a water and sewer bill? And I never got the actual bill. Like, ever.
Okay, I can look into that. Can I get your name and the account name or service address?
It's Diane Iannuccilli. I-A-N-N-U-C-C-I-L-L-I. And I'd rather not do the address thing, I mean, I can give you the account number off the notice? It's right here.
That works. Go ahead with the account number.
Okay, it says four, four, one, seven, dash, zero, three. Then a two. Is that enough?

Let me pull that up. One moment. [pause] Okay, I have it. I see the account under your name, and the notice that went out is a past-due reminder. Can you confirm the mailing address you currently receive mail at?
Well, that's the thing. It's not the one on the notice. The reminder went to my old place? A friend still there forwarded it to me. So that's the only reason I know about any of this.
I see. The mailing address on the account is the previous one. It looks like it was never updated in our system when you moved.

Totally, but I filled out something when I moved, I thought? Like I thought that was handled. Anyway, so the original bill went to the old address and I never saw it. And now I'm getting a past-due notice for something I didn't even know about. Which is, like, annoying.
I understand. I'm showing the original bill was issued about two months ago, and the reminder was generated after the due date passed. Both were mailed to the old address.
Okay. And the amount is way high? Like, the amount on this thing is a lot more than I expected. Last year my winter bills were so much lower. Like barely anything.
Let me look at the usage history. [pause] I can see last winter's readings. The prior winter bills were lower, yes. This latest one reflects a higher consumption reading for the period.
Higher how? Because I'm one person. I'm not, like, filling a pool.

The reading for this period is noticeably higher than the same period last year. I can't tell from here what caused it. It could be an estimated reading that was then corrected, a leak, or a meter issue, but I'd only be speculating.
Okay, so which one is it? Because that's kind of the whole question?
The record doesn't say whether the reading was estimated or actual. That's something the meter team would have to confirm. I can send a request to have the reading verified.
Yeah, please do that. And, um, hold on, sorry, I just got this new cookbook today and I'm flipping through it while I wait. Sorry, it's kind of distracting. Okay. Go ahead.
No problem. I'll put in a request for a reading verification on the account. Someone from that team will review it and follow up. Do you have a good callback number?
Yeah, it's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-eight.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-eight-eight. Got it. I'll also update the mailing address on the account today so future bills reach you. What's the correct address?
Okay, it's a P.O. box now, actually. Is that allowed? Because I'm kind of between places, and honestly I'd rather not say the street.
A mailing address can be a P.O. box. Go ahead and give me the box information.
Box two-two-six, Newport, Rhode Island, zero-two-eight-four-oh.
Box two twenty-six, Newport, zero-two-eight-four-oh. I've updated that.

Great. Now, can you put all this in writing? Like, the explanation, that the bill went to the wrong address, and that you're checking the reading? Because I don't want a late fee on something I never got.

I can send you a written summary of what we discussed: that the bills were mailed to the prior address, that the address has been corrected, and that a reading verification was requested. It will go to the new mailing address.
Okay, and will it say that the late thing is on hold? Because that's the main thing.

I can note on the account that you're disputing the charge pending the verification. Whether any late charge is adjusted would be decided after the review, so I won't put a promise in the letter. It will say the dispute is noted.
Hm. Okay. That's, like, not totally what I wanted, but fine. As long as the dispute is on the record.
It will be. I'm adding the note now. [pause] Done. The summary should go out in the next few business days.
Okay. And how long does the meter team usually take? Roughly?

I don't have a firm timeframe from here. They'll call the number you gave me. If you haven't heard anything in a couple of weeks, call back and reference your account number and I can check the request.
Okay, a couple weeks. Got it. Alright, well, thanks, I guess. It's just annoying to find out like this.
I understand, and I'm sorry about the mix-up with the address. Is there anything else I can help with?
No, that's it. Thanks.
You're welcome, Ms. Iannuccilli. Have a good evening.
